rows.label: Concept
rows.text: s orbitals: spherical, 1 per shell, 2 e⁻, radial nodes = n-1, non-directional, high penetration. p orbitals: dumbbell, 3 per shell (px, py, pz), 6 e⁻, 1 angular node (nodal plane: px→yz, py→xz, pz→xy), directional, forms π bonds. Nodes: radial = n-l-1, angular = l, total = n-1. Penetration: s > p > d > f → energy s < p < d < f (same n). Radial probability P(r) = 4πr²|R|²; peak at r_mp = n²a₀/Z.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Radial nodes = n - l - 1
Angular nodes = l
Total nodes = n - 1

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ s orbital has no radial nodes. ✅ 1s: 0; 2s: 1; 3s: 2; radial nodes = n-1.  ·  ❌ p orbital has no radial nodes. ✅ 2p: 0; 3p: 1; 4p: 2; radial nodes = n-2.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: s orbital: spherical, 1 per shell, 2 e⁻, radial nodes = n-1, angular = 0.  ·  p orbital: dumbbell, 3 per shell (px, py, pz), 6 e⁻, 1 angular node (nodal plane).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: 3p: 1 radial node, 1 angular node (nodal plane), total 2 nodes.  ·  4s: 3 radial nodes, 0 angular nodes, total 3 nodes.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: s and p orbital shapes, nodes, penetration, radial probability, box diagrams (within Atomic Structure).  ·  Out of scope: d/f orbital shapes, detailed hybridization, MO theory — later units.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: s: spherical, 1 per shell, 2 e⁻, radial nodes n-1, non-directional, high penetration.  ·  p: dumbbell, 3 per shell (px, py, pz), 6 e⁻, 1 nodal plane each.  ·  Penetration s > p > d > f → energy s < p < d < f (same n).  ·  Radial probability P(r) = 4πr²|R|²; peak at r_mp = n²a₀/Z.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Radial probability: P(r) = 4πr²|R|²; peak at r_mp = n²a₀/Z.  ·  Box diagram: n+l rule; Hund's (singly first, parallel); Pauli (max 2 opposite).

rows.text: # Orbitals and shape of s and p orbitals only ## 1. Topic Introduction An **orbital** is the region in space where the probability of finding an electron is maximum — a three-dimensional standing wave of the electron's matter wave. Unlike Bohr's definite circular orbits, orbitals are probability clouds described by the wave function ψ.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Conceptual Understanding ### What an orbital is An orbital is a three-dimensional region in space where the probability of finding an electron (|ψ|²) is high (>90%). It is the solution of the Schrödinger equation for the hydrogen atom, characterized by three quantum numbers (n, l, mₗ).…  ·  ## 3. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: P(r) = 4πr²|R(r)|² dr (radial probability)  ·  r_mp = n²a₀/Z (most probable radius for hydrogen-like)  ·  Penetration order: s > p > d > f

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Energy order (same n): E(s) < E(p) < E(d) < E(f)  ·  Box diagram: max 2 e⁻ per box (Pauli); singly first, parallel (Hund); n+l rule (Aufbau)  ·  Paramagnetic: unpaired e⁻ (u > 0); μ = √[u(u+2)] BM

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Diamagnetic: all paired (u = 0)  ·  Paramagnetic = unpaired e⁻; Diamagnetic = all paired.  ·  ❌ All three p orbitals share the same nodal plane. ✅ px→yz, py→xz, pz→xy — different planes.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ s and p orbitals have the same energy in the same shell. ✅ s < p due to penetration.  ·  ❌ Box diagram: pair electrons before filling all degenerate orbitals. ✅ Hund's rule: singly first, parallel spins.  ·  ❌ Radial probability peak for s orbital is at the nucleus. ✅ 1s radial probability peaks at a₀; |ψ|² max at nucleus.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Fe³⁺ (3d⁵): 5 unpaired, μ = √35 ≈ 5.92 BM (paramagnetic).  ·  O₂: π* has 2 unpaired → paramagnetic.  ·  SHORT (3 marks): Write the electronic configuration of N (Z=7) using box diagram.
